input.content: GOAL: read the four frozen evidence bundles and the shared probes before ranking. READ: all four bundles (9637a2495b60c669, 634a0d7731a5d022, dfec9cb5b35ea444, 6476469bc16f6590). OBSERVED: all four are IN SCOPE (behaviour signal + explicit curved op + one coupled pathway + three switches + cost). Frozen baseline Stage3 recall@10 0.055537, support 247/7414/20223; prior radius-spending round collapsed to 2/13/56, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, recall 0.041888. Key probes: E8 K=16/32/64/256 pair-sharing 0.3106/0.2164/0.1547/0.0822; E6 best width-20 recall 0.06363 (resample), 0.06233 (l1_only), 0.06207 (l1_br_euclid), while successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500; E7 good-config NLL 0/3.22/4.36/1.23 (T3 hardest); E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs null 0.067. STILL OPEN: final ordering.

GOAL: place the four proposals against the probes. REASONING: (a) CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL acts only on levels 2-3 where E7 shows the NLL bottleneck (T3=4.36, T4=1.23), keeps level 1 Euclidean so it cannot worsen E8's K=256 first-level capacity ceiling, preserves residual norm and the whole codebook so the 247/7414/20223 export is safe, and is the cheapest (0.2-0.5% step). Caution: E6 tangent_successor_residual already scored 0.05500. (b) CURVCHART-RESGUARD puts a statistically stable per-code curvature on the 24556-node item graph (more data per code than sparse prefix quotients), keeps the codebook byte-identical, and the [0.5,2] guard band bounds regression; but bounded perturbations are the family that E6 successor_geodesic_coarse/v2 already sat at ~0.055. (c) CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN forces 256-way uniform usage: it misreads the inherited baseline as collapsed (247/256 already alive, the 2/256 was the failed prior arm), so it has no resolution headroom, and forcing uniform 256 directly contradicts E8 (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822) which is what width-20 prefix survival needs; also heaviest machinery with 20-epoch lag. (d) CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN freezes column marginals to the Euclidean counts, so it only permutes items within the same K=256 capacity ceiling and cannot coarsen; the argmax of a coupling does not actually preserve those marginals; it is the most expensive (up to 1.8x step) and its family is the one E6 shows at baseline. STILL OPEN: whether CURVCAP or EQUIMARGIN is last.

GOAL: finalise order. DECISION: CURVCAP last because it combines no granularity change (E8 ceiling untouched), a broken capacity-guarantee (argmax of a Sinkhorn coupling need not reproduce the column counts), and the highest cost; EQUIMARGIN third because although hard uniform marginals could echo the best probe (resample 0.06363) it is built on a misdiagnosis (baseline is not collapsed) and its uniformisation runs against E8. Final order: 1 CURVEBEND, 2 CURVCHART-RESGUARD, 3 CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN, 4 CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN. This is the complete answer; no ablation/model run is needed for the review.

part.text:
RANK: CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL | position=1 | reason=E7 puts the hard positions at T3/T4 (NLL 4.36/1.23 in the healthy l1_br_euclid config) and this is the only proposal that acts on exactly levels 2-3 while leaving level 1 Euclidean, so it cannot worsen the E8 K=256 first-level capacity ceiling (0.0822); it preserves residual norm and the whole codebook, guaranteeing the safe 247/7414/20223 export instead of the failed 2/13/56 collapse, and at 0.2-0.5% step cost it is the cheapest clean coupling; the E6 warning is that tangent_successor_residual already scored 0.05500.
RANK: CURVCHART-RESGUARD | position=2 | reason=Its curvature is estimated on the 24556-node training item-transition graph and averaged per codeword, which is statistically far better supported than the sparse prefix-quotient estimates the alternatives rely on, and the codebook is kept byte-identical so the 247/7414/20223 resolution cannot regress toward the 2/13/56 collapse; however the [0.5,2] guard band makes it a bounded perturbation, and E6 shows the equivalent family (successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, v2 0.05463) already sat at the frozen baseline, so upside looks baseline-limited.
RANK: CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ | position=3 | reason=Hard uniform marginals are the one lever that could mirror the best observed width-20 probe (resample recall 0.06363, target SID in beams 0.0884), but E8 says the surviving structure needs small K (0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256), so forcing all 256 codes to equal usage pushes against the very capacity ceiling that governs prefix survival; it also misdiagnoses the inherited baseline as collapsed (2/256 was the failed arm, not the 247/256 baseline), leaving no real resolution headroom, and adds the heaviest machinery (8 Sinkhorn sweeps, 150 quotient-graph syncs, 20-epoch feedback lag).
RANK: CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN | position=4 | reason=Freezing column marginals to the Euclidean nearest-code counts means it can only permute items inside the same K=256 partition, which E8 identifies as the binding capacity limit, so it cannot coarsen or otherwise lift prefix sharing; the claimed resolution guarantee is also unsound because the per-row argmax of a doubly-marginal Sinkhorn coupling need not reproduce the target column counts; and it is the most expensive option (up to 1.8x step, 10 iterations), in the successor-geodesic family that E6 already measured at baseline (0.05500).
